findings.title: Second downsize definition discards the width/height API
findings.body: Ruby has no overloading, so the second OptimizedImage.downsize at app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 replaces the width/height method just above it at line 145 (Ruby warns "method redefined; discarding old downsize"). The wrapper that would build a "#{max_width}x#{max_height}" geometry is therefore dead, and the previous public signature downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) no longer exists. This pull request does not update any other call sites. A caller that still passes an options hash as a fifth argument raises ArgumentError (5 for 4). A four-argument call such as downsize(from, to, 400, 300) binds 400 as the geometry string and 300 as opts, so ImageMagick shrinks to width 400 instead of 400x300, and opts[:allow_animation] raises TypeError because opts is an Integer. optimize was also changed from separate width and height arguments to a single dimensions string, so direct callers of optimize break the same way. Keep one method that accepts either a geometry string or numeric width and height, and update every caller.

findings.title: In-place downsize runs on an extensionless tempfile
findings.body: create_upload downsizes with OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails) at uploads_controller.rb:67. Input and output are the same path. ImageMagick does not support that: convert can truncate the destination before it finishes reading, leaving a zero-byte or corrupt image, and the original bytes are already overwritten so there is no fallback. The false return value is ignored, so Upload.create_for on line 72 stores the damaged file. The path is also the wrong file identity. Rack multipart tempfiles are named like /tmp/RackMultipart... with no suffix, and the URL download uses the prefix discourse-upload-#{type} rather than the real extension; the original name lives only in filename. ImageMagick picks the output coder from the destination suffix, so the write can fail with no encode delegate or emit bytes that do not match filename and content_type. Animation is dropped for the same reason: OptimizedImage.optimize (optimized_image.rb:155) adds the gifsicle path only when the path matches /\.GIF$/i. An extensionless tempfile never matches, so every oversized GIF goes through convert ...[0], which keeps only the first frame. allow_animated_thumbnails therefore cannot preserve animation. Even if the path ended in .gif, gifsicle --resize-fit (optimized_image.rb:120) expects pixel geometry such as 100x100, not ImageMagick's 80%, so that branch would fail too. Tempfile#size is an fstat of the still-open descriptor; if convert replaces the path by rename, the size loop and the filesize passed to create_for keep seeing the old inode. Downsize into a new tempfile that keeps the original extension, and only replace the upload if the command succeeds and the new file is non-empty.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB cap ignores image and attachment settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile used to limit uploads with Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] (max_image_size_kb for images, max_attachment_size_kb for everything else). Line 182 now hardcodes 10 * 1024 KB for both types. Attachments are not downsized, and UploadsController never reads max_attachment_size_kb, so the browser will accept attachments the admin setting forbids (they fail late, or are stored if nothing else checks) and will reject attachments larger than 10MB even when that setting allows them. Images are capped at 10MB even when max_image_size_kb is higher, so previously valid uploads never reach the server downsize path. If max_image_size_kb is already at least 10240, a browser upload can never exceed the server downsize threshold and this feature does not run for normal uploads. The same magic number is repeated in the HTTP 413 alert (utilities.js:246), which tells the user the limit is 10240 KB regardless of the web server or site setting, and in API URL fetches (uploads_controller.rb:55, FileHelper.download(..., 10.megabytes)), which used to stop at SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes and now always pulls up to 10MB, including non-images. The client cap, the 413 text, and the download ceiling need to come from site settings: a real pre-downsize image ceiling, and max_attachment_size_kb for other files.

findings.title: Downsize loop can finish still over the limit
findings.body: The loop at uploads_controller.rb:66 calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times and ignores a false return. convert_with returns false when ImageMagick or gifsicle exits non-zero or ImageOptim raises, and it throws away stderr (&> /dev/null), so a failed pass leaves the file unchanged or truncated while the loop only decrements attempt. It then always calls Upload.create_for with no check that the file is under SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Each pass is a relative 80% geometry shrink plus another lossy re-encode and ImageOptim run, not a resize aimed at the byte limit. Five passes leave about 33% of the linear dimensions (about 10% of the pixels), which is not enough when the upload is near the new 10MB client ceiling and max_image_size_kb is much smaller. The while condition uses tempfile.size, which will not change if the tool replaced the path and the open descriptor still stats the old inode, so all five attempts run anyway. Multipart uploads also have no upper bound before convert, unlike the 10MB URL download, so any logged-in user who can post a large body can force five ImageMagick plus ImageOptim runs on an arbitrarily large image (and on a small decompression bomb just over the setting) on the synchronous request thread or on Scheduler::Defer. Stop when downsize fails, return an error if the file is still over the limit, and refuse files above a hard maximum before invoking convert.

findings.title: No tests for downsizing or the new size caps
findings.body: The new downsize loop in UploadsController#create_upload and the client/API limit changes ship with no tests. Nothing covers an image over max_image_size_kb being stored under that limit, convert failing or still being over the limit after five passes, an animated GIF keeping or losing frames, attachments still honoring max_attachment_size_kb, or OptimizedImage.downsize accepting both a geometry string and numeric width/height. Those are the paths this change gets wrong, and they will not be caught before merge.
